nct.text: Not stated; conducted under Expanded Access IND 78861

citations.quote: the Applicant conducted a new prospective clinical study (Study #18) under the Expanded Access IND 78861 for ^{18}\text{F}-FDOPA at the Feinstein Institutes.

phase.text: Prospective single-center imaging study (adequate and well-controlled)

citations.quote: Study #18 was a prospective, single center study.

design.text: Prospective, single-center study in which binary interpretations of 18F-FDOPA scans by 3 independent blinded readers were analyzed for agreement with a clinical reference standard of PS or non-PS, established by a minimum of 6 months of patient follow-up by a blinded movement disorder specialist.

citations.quote: Study #18 was a prospective, single center study. Binary interpretations of 18F-FDOPA scans by 3 independent readers were analyzed for agreement with a clinical reference standard of PS or non-PS, as established by a minimum of 6 months of patient follow-up.

A clinical reference standard was established in 56 patients with suspected PS through at least 6 months of clinical follow-up by a movement disorder specialist who remained blinded to 18F-FDOPA PET results.

population.text: Adult patients (18 years or older) with at least one cardinal symptom of PS (bradykinesia, rigidity, tremor, postural instability) referred for further evaluation due to diagnostic uncertainty; of 56 completers, 38 (68%) male, 18 (32%) female, mean age 66 years.

citations.quote: Enrollment Criteria: All patients had to be 18 years of age or older with at least one of the cardinal symptoms of PS (defined by the Applicant as bradykinesia, rigidity, tremor, and postural instability).
Among the 56 patients who completed the study, 38 (68%) were male, 18 (32%) were female. Mean age was 66 years.

endpoint.text: Primary endpoints were positive percent agreement (PPA) and negative percent agreement (NPA) between binary 18F-FDOPA PET results and the binary clinical reference standard diagnosis (PS or non-PS) at follow-up.

citations.quote: The primary endpoints of Study #18 were positive percent agreement (PPA) and negative percent agreement (NPA) between binary 18F-FDOPA PET results (positive or negative) and the binary reference standard clinical diagnosis at follow-up (PS or non-PS).

n.text: 56 patients completed at least 6-month follow-up and were included in the efficacy analysis (68 underwent 18F-FDOPA of 69 recruited)

citations.quote: Out of the 69 recruited patients, 68 patients underwent ^{18}\text{F}-FDOPA and 56 completed at least 6-month follow-up clinical assessment to establish the reference standard.

result.text: Across the 3 readers (n=56), NPA ranged 83–91% and PPA ranged 49–73%: Reader 1 PPA 73 (95% CI 55, 87), NPA 91 (72, 99); Reader 2 PPA 49 (31, 67), NPA 91 (72, 99); Reader 3 PPA 58 (39, 75), NPA 83 (61, 94).

citations.quote: High negative percent agreement (point estimate range of 83% to 91%) and lower positive percent agreement (point estimate range of 49% to 73%) were obtained, confirming that ^{18}\text{F}-FDOPA PET can be used as an adjunct to other diagnostic evaluations.

indication.text: Indicated for use in positron emission tomography (PET) to visualize dopaminergic nerve terminals in the striatum for the evaluation of adult patients with suspected Parkinsonian syndromes (PS); PET is an adjunct to other diagnostic evaluations.

citations.quote: Fluorodopa F 18 Injection is indicated for use in positron emission tomography (PET) to visualize dopaminergic nerve terminals in the striatum for the evaluation of adult patients with suspected Parkinsonian syndromes (PS). Fluorodopa F 18 PET is an adjunct to other diagnostic evaluations.

target_moa.text: 18F-FDOPA is a radiolabeled analog of levodopa that crosses the blood-brain barrier and is converted to F-18 fluorodopamine by aromatic amino acid decarboxylase (AAAD) in the striatum, where it is stored in vesicles of dopaminergic neuron terminals; in PS, striatal uptake/storage is reduced, so it acts as a marker of dopaminergic neurodegeneration on PET.

citations.quote: Fluorodopa F 18 injection (18F-FDOPA) is a PET radiopharmaceutical that crosses the blood-brain barrier and is converted to F-18 fluorodopamine by aromatic amino acid decarboxylase (AAAD) in the striatum. The resultant F-18 fluorodopamine is then stored in the vesicles of the striatal terminals of dopaminergic neurons.

The mechanism of 18F-FDOPA allows it to act as a marker of dopaminergic neurodegeneration when imaged by PET. In the setting of PS, the uptake and storage of 18F-FDOPA in the striatum will be reduced.

modality.text: Radiopharmaceutical (PET radiodiagnostic; F-18 radiolabeled analog of levodopa)

citations.quote: Fluorodopa F 18 injection (18F-FDOPA) is a PET radiopharmaceutical that crosses the blood-brain barrier and is converted to F-18 fluorodopamine by aromatic amino acid decarboxylase (AAAD) in the striatum.

key_safety.text: No adverse reactions reported in the open-label trial of 68 patients (plus 53 additional exposures). In Study #18, all 12 observed adverse events (e.g., headache n=2, tiredness n=3) were mild, non-serious, resolved without intervention, and assessed as unlikely related; no deaths or serious AEs. Injection site pain identified in foreign postmarketing experience.

citations.quote: No adverse reactions have been reported for Fluorodopa F 18 Injection based on an open-label clinical trial in 68 patients [*see Clinical Studies (14)*] and additional clinical experience in 53 patients.

There were no deaths or serious adverse events observed. All 12 observed adverse events (AEs) were mild in severity and resolved without intervention. The principal investigator assessed all AEs as unlikely to be related 18F-FDOPA.

basis.text: The prior submission's clinical data (a retrospective chart review of 185 patients) were found inadequate to support the proposed indication; FDA recommended a prospective clinical study.

citations.quote: The submitted clinical data was based on a retrospective chart review of 185 patients at the Applicant's institution. FDA review found the submitted clinical data to be inadequate to support the proposed indication and issued a Complete Response (CR) letter dated 10/22/2013. The FDA recommended that the Applicant conduct a prospective clinical study to support the proposed indication.

summary.text: 18F-FDOPA was approved as a 505(b)(2) NDA (NDA 200655) reviewed as a Class 2 Resubmission responding to a prior Complete Response letter; approval was based on prospective Study #18. No REMS and no postmarketing requirements or commitments were required, and the application was not referred to an advisory committee.
